3.  24-55431  Recommendation to receive and file the Brown Act and Roberts Rules
  presentation by Anita Lakhani from the City Attorney’s office.

  • City Attorney Anita Lakhani delivered an overview of the Brown Act,
  including its history and the general principles of the Ralph M. Brown Act.
  • Additional topics covered included the individuals subject to the Brown Act,
  the types of communications that are restricted, and examples of such
  communications. We also discussed permissible communications,
  requirements for agenda postings, meeting locations, and public rights.
  • The presentation concluded with a discussion of the chair's role during
  discussions, motions, and calls for votes.
  • Small tweaks to a motion can be done as a friendly amendment but must be
  approved by the first and the second.
  • A public comment raised a question about whether a tie vote can be broken
  by the chair?
  • Committee members, staff, and City Attorney Anita participated in further
  discussions regarding the presentation.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Lewis, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Lewis, Lie, Russell, Hilliard
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Rew, Killion, Wood

4.  24-55432  Recommendation to receive and file the Harm Reduction and the HIV/STI Strategic
  Plan presentation by Ismael Salamanca from the Health Department.

  • Ismael Salamanca delivered a comprehensive presentation on Harm
  Reduction and the strategic plan for HIV/STI reduction.
  • He presented background information and data on opioid-related overdoses,
  as well as details on how to administer Narcan. Staff members who use
  Narcan in first aid emergencies are protected under the Good Samaritan
  Law.
  • Ismael concluded the presentation by providing information on how to
  access harm reduction supplies and identifying the signs and symptoms of a
  potential overdose.
  • A member of the public shared concerns about un-housed individuals living
  on the sidewalks in Long Beach, noting the difficulty in distinguishing
  between someone who is sleeping and someone who may be overdosed.

  A motion was made by Member Lewis, seconded by Member Howat, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Lewis, Lie, Russell, Hilliard
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Rew, Killion, Wood

5.  24-55433  Recommendation to receive and file updates from the Mayor’s Fund and Policy
  Subcommittee and the Continuum of Care (CoC) HSAC representative.

  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee Update
  • Commissioner Kimberly discussed changes and design updates for the utility
  bill insert. The subcommittee is developing a presentation to showcase the
  organizations supported by the Mayor’s Fund, which will be featured in the
  press telegram.
  • The draft of the Standard Operating Procedures was examined for final
  revisions and is set to be approved at the November meeting.
  • The subcommittee met with Hali and Erin from His Little Feet to discuss their
  application for the Mayor’s Fund and to clarify additional questions about the
  organization. The subcommittee decided to approve the application.
  Policy Subcommittee Update
  • Commissioner Sarah Bedy provided the update.
  • The committee did not meet in the month of October, the next scheduled
  meeting will be in November.
  CoC Updates

8.  24-55443  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff
  Operations and Updates Report by Paul Duncan from the Health Department.

  • Paul Duncan from the Health Department shared staffing updates,
  highlighting that the team is prioritizing the hiring and interviewing of staff in
  DHHS affected by the expiration of grant funding.
  • On October 29, the Governor announced HHAP Round 5 awards, with Long
  Beach set to receive over $15 million in additional funding.
  • Staff submitted the Long Beach Consolidated Application to HUD on behalf
  of the CoC.
  • Award notices for ERF Round 3 are expected to be announced within the
  next month.
  • The city continues to explore potential projects and opportunities through
  Proposition 1.
  • In partnership with the LA County Homeless Initiative, the Pathway Home
  project successfully resolved the encampment at Veteran’s Park.
  • The admin and operations staff have relocated to the Housing Authority
  building.
  • A new contractor has been selected for roofing and mechanical work at the
  MSC, with work scheduled to begin next year.
  • Staff will monitor the outcomes of County Measure A and its potential
  impacts, with indications suggesting it will pass.
  • Alvin Teng from the City Manager's Office of Homeless Strategy and
  Partnerships provided an update on the city’s approach to Proposition 1,
  detailing plans to submit two proposals due in December: one for a step-
  down residential treatment facility at 702 and another for an expansion of the
  MSC.
  • Commissioners and staff engage in conversation around Alvin’s update
  regarding Prop 1.
  • Member of the public would like clarification on the encampment resolution
  project.
